plain_text:
A heart attack occurs when the flow of oxygenated
blood suddenly becomes blocked, and a section
of the heart can't get oxygen. If blood flow isn't
restored quickly, that section of heart muscle
begins to die. Here's what to look for and what to
do in the case of a heart attack.
semantic_text: A heart attack occurs when the flow of oxygenated blood suddenly becomes blocked, and a section of the heart can't get oxygen. If blood flow isn't restored quickly, that section of heart muscle begins to die. Here's what to look for and what to do in the case of a heart attack.

plain_text:
● Chest pain or discomfort, often on the left
side of the chest
● Light-headedness or dizziness
● Pain or discomfort in the jaw, neck, or back
● Pain or discomfort in one or both arms
or shoulders
● Shortness of breath
● Unexplained tiredness
● Indigestion or heartburn
● Nausea or vomiting
● Sweating

plain_text:
Call 9-1-1 immediately. The sooner the individual
can get to an emergency room, the better their
chances for reducing damage to the heart. If the
individual is unconscious and not breathing or
without a pulse, begin CPR. Push down hard on
the center of the person's chest at about 100 to
120 compressions a minute – about the same
tempo as the Bee Gees' "Staying Alive" or the
Spice Girls' "Wannabe."

plain_text:
Cardiovascular diseases affect the heart and blood
vessels. Some cardiovascular diseases include
coronary artery disease (where the arteries to the
heart are blocked or narrowed), congestive heart
failure (where the heart doesn't pump as efficiently
as it should), and heart rhythm problems.

plain_text:
Heart disease is the leading cause of death for
men, women, and people of most racial and
ethnic groups in the United States.

plain_text:
90—The number of people in the
United States who suffer from
a heart attack every hour.

plain_text:
659,000—The number of people
in the United States who die
from heart disease every year.
semantic_text: 659,000—The number of people in the United States who die from heart disease every year.

plain_text:
$363 billion—The annual cost of
heart disease in the United States.
semantic_text: $363 billion—The annual cost of heart disease in the United States.

plain_text:
80%—The amount of all heart
disease that can be prevented
by keeping a healthy lifestyle and
managing risk factors.
